vocab.kidDefinition: a little box that keeps a light safe from the wind
waiting without getting cross about it
the small rings water makes when something touches it

pages.text: Rosa was not a patient girl, and she knew it. Grandma June said patience was something you grew, like a bean. Rosa had planted hers. It was taking ages.
At the end of the lane was Round Pond, and at the edge of Round Pond was a lantern on a post. Nobody knew who lit it. It was simply lit, every evening, before the dark arrived.

"I want to see who does it," said Rosa.
"Then you'll have to wait," said Grandma June. "That's the whole of it."
So Rosa waited. She waited through the geese going over. She waited through the light going the colour of honey, and then the colour of tea.
A frog considered her from a stone. A dragonfly stitched the air. The pond went quiet in the way water does when it is thinking.

And then, without any fuss at all, the lantern lit.

Rosa had been looking right at it. She had not seen a hand, or a match, or a single ripple on the water.
She sat with that for a while. Some things, she decided, are not for catching. Some things are only for being there when they happen.

Grandma June was on the step when Rosa came up the lane in the blue dark.

"Well?" she said.

"I waited," said Rosa. And that, it turned out, was the answer.
